frame.grid.note: recorded for provenance/auditing ONLY. This digest is NEVER a gate predicate: llvmpipe is not bit-reproducible and this scenario own sweep produced 10 distinct grid digests over 10 BYTE-IDENTICAL dumps. Byte-hashing the frame would make the gate flake on renderer noise. The dump is hashed byte-wise because it is quantised and deterministic; the frame is not. The asymmetry is deliberate.

margin.reading: the blessed frame clears the floor by 2.6x and same-scene noise is 0.08x the floor, so no same-scene variation can push a real frame under it and an empty render (distance 0) cannot climb over it.

frame_liveness.what_it_proves: that something was RENDERED - the property a dead run fails. Asserted IN ADDITION to the tolerance, not instead of it: a frame can be within tolerance of a reference that was itself black, so liveness is checked against an absolute.

frame_measurements.separation_reading: min(wrong-scene distance) / max(same-scene distance). Above 1 means the observable can discriminate; scenario 015 measured 0.25 and could not. Bead oo-gxp scenario 010 reached 261.

frame_tolerance.tolerance_source: tests/golden/frame_hash.py derive_tolerance() over tests/golden/calibration.json (bead oo-ae9). USED AS MEASURED, never adjusted to make a run pass.
frame_tolerance.why_asserted: MEASURED AND ACCEPTED, unlike scenario 015. That scenario frame animates (HeadUpDisplay.m:3306 -drawTrumbles: redraws a live population every frame with randf()-scheduled animations) and its same-scene pairs sat at 1.08x..2.49x the tolerance - signal smaller than noise, so it could assert only liveness. THIS scenario docked scene is static: all 45 same-scene pairs over the 10-run sweep span 0.001367..0.001545, i.e. 0.31x..0.35x the tolerance, with a 2.8x margin under it, while a DIFFERENT scene (scenario 015 blessed Lave frame) sits at 0.025080, 5.7x the tolerance and 16x the largest same-scene distance. Separation ratio 16.2: the observable discriminates, so the tolerance is asserted.

landing_rehearsal.note: Both the gate and the offline tests search goldens/windows-x64/017-thargoid-plans/ FIRST and fall back to tests/golden/pending/017-thargoid-plans/, through the identical idiom, so landing is a pure `git mv` with no code change. REHEARSED FOR REAL in a scratch worktree: the move was performed and every stored acceptance line re-run green afterwards. See LANDING.md.

mission_variable_assertion.why: CHECKED BEFORE THE ASSERTION WAS DESIGNED. Scenario 015 fixture holds mission_trumbles as the EMPTY STRING and an ABSENT mission variable reads identically over the JS bridge, so that scenario could assert only a key SET. Every one of THIS fixture five values is a non-empty string, so the whole map is asserted - strictly stronger, and it pins conhunt == MISSION_COMPLETE. saved_mission_variables() REFUSES (rc=2) if a future fixture ever carries an empty value, rather than keeping a check that cannot fail.

save_format_contract.discovered_by: MEASURED, not read off the source first: the scenario first live run went red with `credits: 99454.7 (saved) != 100354.7 (loaded)`, a delta of exactly 9000 plist units, and the log named the cause.
save_format_contract.handled_by: spec.load_migrations declares the delta; thargoid_plans_load.apply_load_migrations() adds it to the FILE side so the round trip stays an EXACT equality. A tolerance was REJECTED: widening credits by 900 would hide any credit bug smaller than 900 credits, which is most of them. The engine OWN log line is required as evidence (evidence.load_upgrade_messages) so the adjustment is falsifiable rather than a fudge factor.
save_format_contract.migration: PlayerEntity.m:1731-1746. The fixture carries has_energy_bomb=true and EQ_ENERGY_BOMB, equipment that no longer exists. The loader tries to mount an EQ_QC_MINE in its place and, failing that (all four pylons already hold EQ_HARDENED_MISSILE), does `credits += 9000` - 9000 DECIcredits, 900 credits - and logs 'Compensated legacy energy bomb with 900 credits.' on the load.upgrade.replacedEnergyBomb channel.

stability.note: ALL TEN runs wrote a BYTE-IDENTICAL dump (3085 bytes, one digest); 0 refused, 0 errored, so dumps_written + refused == runs with nothing unaccounted. The frame grids are all distinct, as expected: llvmpipe is not bit-reproducible, which is why the grid is compared with the measured tolerance and is NOT part of state.json. The blessed state.json is byte-identical to all ten sweep dumps.

thargoid_plans_mission_state.mission_variables_note: MEASURED both before and after the 24-tick budget: identical. A docked player opening no mission screen does not advance the mission, so the dump carries mission_variables_stable_across_ticks and an engine that DID start it here goes red instead of drifting.
thargoid_plans_mission_state.verdict: The bead prose names mission_thargplans; it is ABSENT from this fixture, which sits BEFORE the mission starts. FOUR of oolite-thargoid-plans-mission.js:77-90 five arming clauses hold (conhunt MISSION_COMPLETE, thargplans unset, ship_kills 1281 one over the 1280 threshold, Quedle is system 147 not 83). THE FIFTH DOES NOT: JS galaxyNumber is [player currentGalaxyID] (OOJSGlobal.m:190-191), the SAME 0-based index the plist stores, so this save is in galaxy 1 and the mission runs in galaxy 2. A first draft of this scenario assumed the JS field was 1-based and asserted galaxy_is_two=true; the LIVE RUN DISPROVED IT and the assertion was corrected to the measurement, not the other way round. The fixture carries EQ_GAL_DRIVE and has_galactic_hyperdrive, so it is positioned ONE GALACTIC JUMP SHORT of the mission - which is the step the checklist asks a human tester to perform.
